requirement:
Each listed file provides access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
rationale: The requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` has two obligations. Each listed file must provide access to a file-notes view, and that view must identify the file's workspace-relative path. The reviewed tests cover both. **Access from the file map.** In `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]`, the loop runs over `code.rs`, `src/direct.rs` and `src/deep/nested.rs`. These cover a root file, a file in a directory and a file in a nested directory. - Each file's card must contain an `href` equal to the expected link. The test computes that link with `notes::path` and `chapter_href`. - Each card must also contain per-note anchors of the form `#coverage-note-N`. - A chapter named `File notes: {file}` must exist, and its `path` must equal the computed note path. **Path identification.** The same loop asserts that the notes chapter content contains `File: {file}`, so the view shows the workspace-relative path, including `src/deep/nested.rs`. It also asserts that the note `id="coverage-note-N"` anchors exist. The card location strings also include `{file}:{line}`. **Coverage of every listed file.** The test asserts that exactly 5 `File notes:` chapters exist. That matches the five listed files, including `vendor/foreign.rs` and `docs_only/deep/item.rs`. It excludes `src/pass.rs`, which has no coverage annotations. The per-file link and path assertions run on only three of the five files. The other two follow the same code path, and the requirement draws no distinction for them, so I don't count this as a gap. **Notes page content.** `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` renders a notes page directly. It asserts that the page contains `File: code.rs` and that its sections carry `Source: code.rs:…`. It supports the path-identification obligation. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. No gaps are found.
